explanation: A is correct because a high-fidelity model should match the real business context, including the fact that one customer can hold several plans and one plan can apply to many customers. Modeling that many-to-many relationship preserves the stated facts. B loses valid multiple-plan cases, C collapses two different real-world things into one entity, and D fails to represent an important business relationship at all.

options.text: Model a many-to-many relationship between Customer and Plan.
Store a single Plan attribute in Customer because one current plan is enough for modeling.
Merge Customer and Plan into one entity because they both belong to the membership system.
Omit the relationship until physical database design decides how to store it.

prompt: A membership business has customers and plans. The business rules say a customer may hold multiple plans at the same time, and each plan may be held by many customers. In a conceptual data model, which choice best preserves a high-fidelity representation of this situation?
